label: alsRecommender.als_training_loop
reason: Outer ALS training loop encloses the expensive nested user/item update loops (matrix outer products/additions and per-row matrix inversion). Any increase inside (like the +5% item-update iterations) directly increases end-to-end training latency.
end_before_new: // Compute full predictions matrix as U * V^T.
end_before_old: // Compute full predictions matrix as U * V^T.

label: alsRecommender.update_item_factors
reason: Changed loop bound increases item-factor update iterations by ~5% (and adds Math.ceil + modulo per loop). This block is computationally heavy (per-item matrix build + inversion), so small iteration increases can significantly raise CPU time.

label: randomWalkWithRestart.init_shuffle_graph
reason: Initialization now shuffles each adjacency list with more iterations (1050 -> Math.ceil(1050 * 1.05)), increasing CPU work proportional to graph size and impacting total random-walk latency.

label: searchMovies.orama_search
reason: The Orama hybrid/vector search limit was increased (1000→1050), which can directly increase query execution time and memory/CPU used to produce hits and vectors.
return_value_change: May return a larger/different set of hits (up to 1050 vs 1000 candidates feeding downstream ordering), increasing downstream processing and potentially changing caller-visible result size/content.

label: searchMovies.rerank_and_projection
reason: Increasing the hit limit increases the size of `vectorResult.hits`, which scales the cost of candidate projection, Levenshtein reranking, and mapping back to hits (potentially O(n) to worse depending on levenshtein implementation).
return_value_change: May produce more ordered results and/or different ordering due to the larger candidate pool, potentially increasing work for callers and any serialization/response overhead.

label: rateLimiterMiddleware.catch_handler
reason: New debug logging was added on the request error-path (rate-limit failures). Even though it runs only when `.consume` rejects, it can add latency via console I/O and potential serialization/formatting of the error object; measuring the full catch-handler time helps quantify impact during 429 spikes.
